source: For constant speed, distance equals speed multiplied by elapsed time. Walker A moves at 3 metres per second. Walker B moves at 5 metres per second. After six seconds, A has travelled 18 metres and B has travelled 30 metres. The 12 metre gap comes from their speed difference, 2 metres per second, multiplied by six seconds. Both walkers share the same clock. Equal intervals add equal distances for each walker, but different speeds produce different distances. This model assumes each speed stays constant.
